what: BRAF V600E is a change in the BRAF gene.
This change is the most common BRAF change in many cancers, and it can switch the gene on.
intro.test_report: If a test report mentions BRAF V600E, it is noting this gene change. That note is not a diagnosis, and it is not a decision about treatment.

Atezolizumab (TECENTRIQ): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for melanoma (a skin cancer) with a BRAF V600 change.
Binimetinib (MEKTOVI): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2018.
Cetuximab (ERBITUX): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for advanced bowel cancer with a BRAF V600E change.
Cobimetinib (Cotellic): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for melanoma (a skin cancer) with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2015.
Dabrafenib (Tafinlar): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for melanoma (a skin cancer) with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2013.
Encorafenib (BRAFTOVI): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for advanced bowel cancer with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2018.
Tovorafenib (OJEMDA): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for brain tumour with a BRAF V600 change.
Trametinib (Mekinist): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for melanoma (a skin cancer) with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2020.
Vemurafenib (ZELBORAF): a drug that blocks the BRAF signal. Approved for melanoma (a skin cancer) with a BRAF V600E change. Authorised in Europe since 2011.
